title: Telemetry concordance for model fallbacks and KV-cache affinity
creator: Maya Chen
description: Add an SDK- and runtime-level telemetry concordance mechanism that preserves request identity and provenance across automatic model-variant fallbacks and KV-cache affinity decisions. Purpose is to make traces, metrics, and logs show a unified view when a single logical request invokes multiple model variants or bypasses cache, enabling accurate latency/error attribution, quality regressions, and cost breakdowns.
background_and_motivation: We currently lose clear linkage between the original client request and downstream model-variant decisions (canary fallback, quantized variant, or lower-cost variant) as well as KV-cache interactions. This obscures root cause analysis for latency spikes and functional regressions when runtime routing changes. Support teams and SREs need per-request concordance to explain tail latency and error clusters tied to fallback patterns.
technical_design: Introduce a compact Telemetry Concordance Envelope (TCE) attached as a single header in SDK middleware: tce-bin or tce (base64). Envelope fields: original_request_id, route_generation (int), model_variant_hint, kvcache_affinity_token (opaque short token), and a version tag.

SDK changes: language SDK middleware to stamp TCE on outgoing requests only when sampling or when feature-flag enabled for all requests. Provide deterministic token generation so retries keep the same token. Fall back to header-splitting approach for transports that restrict binary headers.

Runtime changes: serving runtime extracts TCE, propagates concordance to all internal RPCs and worker spans, and emits fields as span attributes: redwood.request.id, redwood.variant.selected, redwood.variant.fallback_reason, redwood.kvcache.hit (bool), redwood.kvcache.affinity_token.

KV-cache affinity: runtime will map kvcache_affinity_token -> logical cache shard in observability telemetry so cache hit/miss metrics can be correlated to variant selection and client request groups.

Fallback attribution: when runtime performs model fallback, it will mark span attribute redwood.variant.fallback_reason with canonical enum (e.g., capacity, latency_sla, error) and increment a dedicated counter with original_request_id tag for debugging.

Compatibility: graceful noop if TCE header missing. Backwards-compatibility shim for older SDKs to accept 'x-redwood-tce' text header. Avoid leaking PII by keeping envelope opaque except for request id and tokens.

Sampling and overhead: envelope is limited to ~80 bytes before base64 to minimize proxy/header issues. SDKs will default to sampled-only stamping for high-throughput customers, with a per-account opt-in flag for full stamping.
Security: envelope contains no secrets. affinity token is opaque and rotates per-connection; optionally HMAC-signed by SDK when account-level integrity is required (opt-in).
acceptance_criteria: Traces emitted for a request that triggers fallback show original_request_id and both initial and fallback model_variant in span attributes
Dashboards can pivot by redwood.variant.selected and filter on redwood.variant.fallback_reason to find clusters
KV-cache hit/miss metrics are correlated with affinity token and show per-shard hit rates in Console
No measurable p99 latency regression > 1ms for common RPC paths when TCE is not enabled; when enabled in sampled mode, overhead <= 2% on tokenized workloads
SDKs across Node, Python, and Go implement TCE middleware with unit tests and e2e test harness
Feature flagged and rolloutable: can be toggled per-org and per-route in Console
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Implement TCE extraction and span-attribute emission in runtime (canary on non-customer traffic). Instrument internal dashboards to surface variant/fallback counters.
Phase 2: Ship SDK middleware as opt-in beta to internal teams and a small set of customers; validate header sizes and proxy behavior.
Phase 3: Enable sampling-by-default for signed-off customers and expose toggles in Console; build runbook for investigating fallback clusters.
Phase 4: Gradually enable full-stamping for customers who opt in; monitor CPU and network overhead metrics for the telemetry pipeline.
Rollback: server-side can drop TCE extraction without SDK changes; SDK default remains noop if server feature is disabled.
testing_plan: Unit tests for SDK middleware: header encoding/decoding, deterministic token generation, retry semantics
Integration test: multi-variant request flow that records initial model choice, fallback, and final selection with span assertions
Performance test: benchmark service p99 with and without TCE enabled on sampled traffic (compare CPU and tail latency)
Chaos test: simulate proxy that truncates headers -> ensure runtime ignores malformed TCE but still continues serving
E2E smoke: validate Console dashboards surface variant/fallback counters and kvcache-affinity pivots
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: some proxies / edge routers may strip or truncate headers -> Mitigation: fallback to text header, enforce base64 length cap, detect truncation and emit diagnostic metric for dropped TCE
Risk: header bloat increases request size -> Mitigation: compact envelope design, sampling, and per-org opt-in
Risk: incorrect attribution if runtime rewrites request ids -> Mitigation: require immutable original_request_id in TCE and validate signing option for enterprise customers

Risk: high-cardinality tokens causing metrics cardinality explosion -> Mitigation: affinity token is opaque short slug (not full request id) and metrics pipeline will aggregate by token bucket and rotate keys

comments: 2026-02-16 Maya Chen: Initial draft of TCE. Focused on minimal envelope to avoid proxy issues.
2026-02-18 Liam O'Connor (PM): Suggested adding explicit fallback_reason enum to simplify dashboard filters. Also requested per-org opt-in control.

2026-02-23 Arjun Patel: Prototype runtime extraction done; emitting redwood.variant.selected and redwood.variant.fallback_reason as span attrs. Observed an edge case where retries generate new IDs; changed token to be retry-deterministic.
2026-03-01 Design review (SREs + SDK): Flagged header length on older corp proxies. Action: add compact text header fallback and test on staging proxies.

2026-03-05 QA: Found increased 504s on a small subset of customers when full-stamping enabled. Root cause: an internal edge filter dropped requests > 8KB headers. Mitigation: cap TCE to 128 bytes encoded and add sampling.
2026-03-09 Code review (runtime): LGTM after small perf micro-optimizations. Runtime side added fast-path to avoid decode when header absent.
2026-03-10 Arjun Patel: Enabling canary on internal non-customer traffic; monitoring hit rates and fallback counters. Next: ship Node and Python SDK middleware as opt-in beta.
next_steps: Finish Node & Python SDK middleware PRs and include automated header-truncation tests
Wire variant/fallback counters into Console and add pivot controls for affinity_token
Run 2-week canary on internal traffic, validate no perf regressions, then invite 3 external beta customers
